prompt: Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: finished illustrated background for an interactive website food map titled KL Food Compass. Generate a richly detailed, delightful 3D isometric toy-construction-brick diorama map of five Kuala Lumpur neighbourhood destinations on one landscaped tabletop island. Landscape image roughly 4:3. This is an environment asset, not a screenshot or UI. Absolutely NO text, NO letters, NO labels, NO title, NO banners, NO signboards, NO floating cards, NO numbers, NO watermark; all interactive labels will be added separately in HTML. Warm cinematic sunshine, matte and glossy ABS interlocking bricks, visible studs, elegant miniature architectural craftsmanship, lush small brick palm trees, little gardens, curving cream streets, a blue-green stream on the western side and a small bridge, friendly magical travel-game look matching a toy-brick train adventure. Muted sage green base, lively coral yellow cream and teal buildings, fine material texture and soft shadows, uncluttered paths and enough quiet greenery for small clickable labels. Full image is the map, with no exterior frame. Important approximate placement of FIVE distinct destination architectural groups, percentage positions measured from image top left: (1) Berjaya Times Square HOME at x58% y43%, a pair of warm golden-orange tall rectangular hotel towers sharing a shopping podium; (2) LalaPort at x34% y64%, a modern low terraced mall with coral facade, broad steps and planted rooftop; (3) Nu Sentral at x12% y77%, a compact modern teal glass shopping mall beside a small train station with a red roof and tiny rails; (4) Pavilion KL at x80% y18%, a cream and pale mint luxury mall with a broad glass atrium and a red plaza; (5) Pudu at x80% y82%, a charming short row of pink and ochre traditional shophouses with striped awnings, representing a dessert neighbourhood. Keep these five groups spatially separated, connected by toy streets and footpaths, easy to distinguish, do not scatter additional large landmarks. North is up. Leave each landmark visible with its surrounding streets. Do not include restaurant brands or fabricated logos. Artwork must feel like an inviting actual toy city on a board, with substantial dimensionality and beautiful brick details.
